instruction: I jotted down some songs in Simple Note recently. Make a playlist titled "Random Playlist" out of it.
notes: Two-app task: read the recent song list from Simple Note, then build a Spotify playlist. The note is found via search_notes (query 'songs', pick the most recent matching note) and its content is read with show_note; only after note-read can each listed song be looked up with spotify.search_songs (no token needed), which asserts known-id for the song. create_playlist is guarded by (not (playlist-created ?p)) so exactly one playlist titled 'Random Playlist' is added, matching the evaluation (only spotify.Playlist and spotify.PlaylistSong change). The number of songs in the note is unknown in advance; the model uses three placeholder songs (song-1..song-3) with corresponding runtime queries, and the count should be adjusted to the actual number of entries in the note. The goal entities (songs, playlist, title) are declared as domain constants so supervisor-complete-task's precondition can state every goal condition explicitly; they are therefore not redeclared in the problem's :objects. The supervisor person object is included by convention but participates in no action. No answer is required, so complete_task takes no parameters.
